correctness.rationale: Equation reduction matches the normalized source ODE with unit self-weights. Exact differentiation conserves \(\operatorname{arctanh}(w)+H(d)\). The scalar potential \(H\) has a unique maximum at the half-interaction crossing, tends to negative infinity at gap zero, and its root geometry classifies all positive initial ties. The quadratic maximum yields gap asymptotic \(1/[-\phi'(r_c)t]\) and tie asymptotic \(1/[r_c(-\phi'(r_c))t^2]\); logarithmic ODE derivatives establish off-critical rates. The packaged numerical solver passed 80 exponential parameter/invariant checks, two critical decay tests, and one rational-kernel three-regime check; finite tests support but do not establish the theorem.

value.rationale: The source’s numerical consensus/polarization transition is sharpened to an exact initial-tie separatrix, with a positive-separation root and universal \(t^{-1}\)/\(t^{-2}\) critical laws and explicit leading coefficients. These are structurally meaningful behavioral distinctions in the smallest adaptive social network, useful as a benchmark for larger-network theory; they are not implied by the published qualitative cluster-limit theorems.
